rationale.text: Delhi--Mumbai uses a carrier service: the inter-site physical layer belongs to the provider, so only the local handoff is designed (Cat6a 10GBASE-T to the demarc, assumed ≤ 100 m).
Delhi--Bengaluru uses a carrier service: the inter-site physical layer belongs to the provider, so only the local handoff is designed (Cat6a 10GBASE-T to the demarc, assumed ≤ 100 m).
Delhi--Singapore uses a internet service: the inter-site physical layer belongs to the provider, so only the local handoff is designed (Cat6a 10GBASE-T to the demarc, assumed ≤ 100 m).
Delhi--CloudVPC uses a internet service: the inter-site physical layer belongs to the provider, so only the local handoff is designed (Cat6a 10GBASE-T to the demarc, assumed ≤ 100 m).
Multi-area OSPF because the design spans 5 sites: Delhi is the backbone (area 0) and every other site gets its own area, so flooding and SPF runs stay inside one site.

Delhi--Singapore runs over the internet, so traffic between DELHI-R1 and SINGAPORE-R1 is encrypted in a route-based IPsec tunnel (VTI, AES-256 / SHA-256, DH group 14). Underlay addresses come from 203.0.113.0/24 (RFC 5737 documentation range): replace them with the real public IPs.

Delhi--CloudVPC runs over the internet, so traffic between DELHI-R1 and CLOUDVPC-VGW is encrypted in a route-based IPsec tunnel (VTI, AES-256 / SHA-256, DH group 14). Underlay addresses come from 203.0.113.0/24 (RFC 5737 documentation range): replace them with the real public IPs.
Area 0 (Delhi) is OSPF area 0 with address block 10.100.0.0/21.
Area 1 (Mumbai) is OSPF area 1 with address block 10.100.8.0/22.
Area 2 (Bengaluru) is OSPF area 2 with address block 10.100.12.0/22.
Area 3 (Singapore) is OSPF area 3 with address block 10.100.16.0/22.
Router IDs come from Loopback0 /32 addresses. A loopback never goes down with a physical interface, so OSPF and BGP identities stay stable.
OSPF reference bandwidth is 100000 Mbps. With the default 100 Mbps every link of 100 Mb/s or more gets cost 1, so 10G and 1G paths would look equal.
ABR MUMBAI-R1 summarizes area 1 as 10.100.8.0/22 (1 route instead of 4), which works because the area's subnets were allocated from one contiguous block.
ABR BENGALURU-R1 summarizes area 2 as 10.100.12.0/22 (1 route instead of 4), which works because the area's subnets were allocated from one contiguous block.
ABR SINGAPORE-R1 summarizes area 3 as 10.100.16.0/22 (1 route instead of 4), which works because the area's subnets were allocated from one contiguous block.

DELHI-R1 anchors its 4 BGP-advertised area block(s) with Null0 static routes at administrative distance 254 (floating). BGP `network` needs an exact route in the RIB, but an AD-1 static would beat the OSPF summary for the same prefix and blackhole remote areas; at AD 254 the static is used only when OSPF has no route.

eBGP between DELHI-R1 (AS 65000) and CLOUDVPC-VGW (AS 65100) because the cloud VPC is a separate administrative domain. BGP keeps policy control at the boundary and OSPF is not extended into the provider. Both ASNs are private (RFC 6996).

rationale.text: Delhi: collapsed-core design (core and distribution combined) because the site has 1 building(s), below the 4-building point where a separate distribution layer pays off. Fewer devices and hops for 600 endpoints.
Delhi: 600 access ports needed, so 13 × 48-port switch(es) in 2 stack(s) (≤ 8 members per stack). 24 spare port(s) are shut down.

Native VLAN is the unused VLAN 999 on every trunk (not VLAN 1) and it is left out of the allowed lists. This blocks double-tagging VLAN hopping. Unused access ports are parked in it and shut down.
Access ports use PortFast (RSTP edge port, forwards immediately) and BPDU Guard (err-disables the port if a switch is plugged in), preventing accidental loops.
Delhi: VLANs 10 each carry one segment, giving each role its own broadcast domain.
DELHI-ACC1 trunk to DELHI-CORE1 allows only VLANs 10, the VLANs that have ports behind it, instead of all 4094. This limits broadcast flooding and blast radius.
DELHI-ACC2 trunk to DELHI-CORE1 allows only VLANs 10, the VLANs that have ports behind it, instead of all 4094. This limits broadcast flooding and blast radius.
Delhi: Rapid PVST+ root primary on DELHI-CORE1, so the root bridge is also the default gateway and frames never take a detour through an access switch.

Sg-IoT → VPC-Apps: permit tcp port 8883 via ACL-SG-IOT-IN, applied inbound on the Sg-IoT gateway so the decision is made at the first layer-3 hop.
Sg-IoT → VPC-Apps: deny ip via ACL-SG-IOT-IN, applied inbound on the Sg-IoT gateway so the decision is made at the first layer-3 hop.
ACL-SG-IOT-IN ends with 'permit ip any any' so traffic not covered by a policy is allowed; otherwise the IOS implicit deny would drop all other traffic from Sg-IoT.
